description: AND, OR, NOT and XOR in truth tables and how to solve logic problems.
content_html:
What Are Logical Operators?

Computers make decisions by evaluating conditions that are either true or false. Logical operators are the building blocks of this decision-making. They combine Boolean values — values that are either 1 (true) or 0 (false) — and produce a Boolean result. In hardware, these operators are implemented as logic gates. In software, they appear inside if statements and while loops. Understanding them is essential for both circuit design and programming.

A truth table is the standard way to describe a logical operator’s behaviour. Each row represents one combination of inputs. For two inputs A and B there are four possible combinations: (0,0), (0,1), (1,0) and (1,1). You must always show every row — leaving rows out drops marks in the exam.

Key Fact

There are four logical operators you need to know: AND, OR, NOT and XOR. Each has a standard symbol used in circuit diagrams and a truth table showing every possible input-output combination.

The AND Operator

AND outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1. Think of it as a strict gatekeeper: every condition must be met. In Boolean notation, AND is written with a dot or by placing letters side by side: A·B or AB.

ABA AND B
000
010
100
111

The OR Operator

OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1. It only outputs 0 when both inputs are 0. In Boolean notation, OR is written with a plus sign: A + B.

ABA OR B
000
011
101
111

The NOT Operator

NOT is a single-input operator that inverts its input: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0. It is also called a complement or inverter. In Boolean notation, NOT is written as an overbar — for example, NOT A is written as Ā (A with an overbar) — or sometimes as A′ or !A.

ANOT A
01
10

The XOR Operator

XOR (exclusive OR) outputs 1 when the inputs are different. If both inputs are the same — both 0 or both 1 — the output is 0. XOR is denoted A ⊕ B. It is particularly useful in binary addition circuits (half adders) and encryption.

ABA XOR B
000
011
101
110
Key Fact

XOR outputs 1 only when its two inputs differ. This distinguishes it from OR: OR outputs 1 when both inputs are 1, but XOR outputs 0 in that case because the inputs are the same.

Real circuits chain several gates together. Consider the expression NOT A AND B. To build the truth table, add an intermediate column for NOT A before the final output column.

ABNOT ANOT A AND B
0010
0111
1000
1100

Notice the extra intermediate column. In the exam, when a question includes a combined circuit, fill in every intermediate column — each cell can earn an independent mark. Do not skip straight to the output column.

The most common error in truth table questions is confusing XOR with OR. Remember: OR outputs 1 for the row (1,1), but XOR outputs 0 for that row because the inputs are the same. Write the row (1,1) carefully for every XOR column.

A second mistake is filling in only the output column for combined-gate questions. The mark scheme awards one mark per correct cell, including intermediate columns. If the question shows a two-stage gate circuit, add an intermediate column for each gate stage and fill every row before moving to the final output.

A third mistake is mixing up Boolean notation with arithmetic. In Boolean expressions, A·B means AND and A + B means OR. The + symbol does NOT mean addition here. Students who confuse arithmetic addition with Boolean OR often get three-variable expressions wrong.

NAND and NOR Gates

Two additional gates appear in this course: NAND and NOR. A NAND gate is AND followed by NOT — its output is the inverse of AND. A NOR gate is OR followed by NOT — its output is the inverse of OR. NAND and NOR are called universal gates because any logic circuit can be built from NAND gates alone (or NOR gates alone).

ABNANDNOR
0011
0110
1010
1100

Notice that NAND outputs 0 only in the last row (both inputs 1), while NOR outputs 1 only in the first row (both inputs 0). These are exactly opposite to AND and OR respectively. The practical importance of universal gates is that hardware manufacturers can produce one type of gate in bulk and use it to build every other gate, simplifying chip design and reducing manufacturing costs.
exam_tip_html: Truth table questions award one mark per correct output cell — not one mark for the whole table. Always write every row, include intermediate columns for combined circuits, and never leave a cell blank. For a two-input truth table, you need exactly four rows. For XOR specifically, double-check the (1,1) row: the output is 0, not 1, because the inputs are the same. In describe or explain questions about logic gates, name the operator (AND/OR/NOT/XOR/NAND/NOR) and state the condition that produces a 1 output.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • AND outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1; OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1; NOT inverts its single input; XOR outputs 1 when inputs differ.
  • For combined-gate truth tables, add an intermediate column for each gate stage and fill every cell — each cell earns an independent mark.
  • NAND and NOR are the inverse of AND and OR respectively, and are called universal gates because any circuit can be built from either one alone.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following correctly describes the output of an XOR gate?
A) Outputs 1 when both inputs are 1
B) Outputs 1 when at least one input is 1
C) Outputs 1 when the two inputs are different
D) Outputs 1 when both inputs are 0
practice_questions.marks: C) Outputs 1 when the two inputs are different [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: State the Boolean notation symbol used to represent the AND operator.
practice_questions.marks: A dot (·) or placing letters side by side, e.g. A·B or AB [1 mark]

practice_questions.text:
Complete the truth table below for the expression NOT A AND B.

A | B | NOT A | NOT A AND B
0 | 0 |       |
0 | 1 |       |
1 | 0 |       |
1 | 1 |       |
practice_questions.marks:
NOT A column: 1, 1, 0, 0 [1 mark]
NOT A AND B column: 0, 1, 0, 0 [1 mark]
Both marks awarded independently per column.

practice_questions.text: Explain the difference between an OR gate and an XOR gate. Use a truth table row to support your answer.
practice_questions.marks: OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1 [1]; this includes the case where both inputs are 1 [1]. XOR outputs 1 only when the inputs are different [1]; when both inputs are 1, XOR outputs 0 [1]. The key distinguishing row is (1,1): OR gives 1, XOR gives 0.

practice_questions.text: A security system uses two sensors, A and B. The alarm triggers (output = 1) only when both sensors detect a problem at the same time. Identify which logic gate models this behaviour and complete a full truth table for it.
practice_questions.marks: Gate identified as AND [1]. Truth table with four rows: (0,0) gives 0, (0,1) gives 0, (1,0) gives 0, (1,1) gives 1 [1 mark per correct row up to 3 marks]. Full marks: all four rows correct and AND identified.

practice_questions.text: Compare how a NAND gate and a NOR gate behave. In your answer, relate each gate to its component parts and explain when each outputs a 0.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: NAND described as AND then NOT — outputs 0 only when both inputs are 1 (unlike AND which outputs 1); NOR described as OR then NOT — outputs 1 only when both inputs are 0; explicit contrast of the two (e.g. unlike NAND, which outputs 0 only in the row where both inputs are 1, NOR outputs 0 in three of four rows); conclusion that both are universal gates.
Secure: Both gates correctly described with their component parts; comparison present but may lack one explicit contrast point.
Developing: One gate correctly described or one contrast made without full explanation.
Emerging: Partial attempt; may confuse NAND with NOR or omit the NOT stage.

knowledge_checks.q: What output does an AND gate produce when A = 1 and B = 0?
Which gate is described as a universal gate because any circuit can be built from it alone?
XOR outputs 1 only when its two inputs are _____.
In Boolean algebra, the + symbol represents the _____ operator.
Match each gate to its rule:
right: Outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1

flashcard_questions.q: What output does an AND gate produce when both A and B are 1?
flashcard_questions.a: 1 — AND only outputs 1 when both inputs are 1.

flashcard_questions.q: An AND gate has inputs A = 1, B = 0. What is the output?
flashcard_questions.a: 0 — AND requires both inputs to be 1.

flashcard_questions.q: What output does an OR gate produce when both inputs are 0?
flashcard_questions.a: 0 — OR outputs 0 only when all inputs are 0.

flashcard_questions.q: Which logical operator does the Boolean expression A + B represent?
Which logical operation does the Boolean expression A·B represent?
A NOT gate receives input 1. What is its output?
What does the overbar notation in Boolean algebra mean, e.g. NOT A written with an overbar?
flashcard_questions.a: The complement (inverse) of A — the NOT operator.

flashcard_questions.q: An XOR gate has inputs A = 1, B = 1. What is the output?
flashcard_questions.a: 0 — XOR outputs 0 when inputs are the same.

flashcard_questions.q: An XOR gate has inputs A = 0, B = 1. What is the output?
Why is XOR used in binary addition circuits?
flashcard_questions.a: It outputs 1 when inputs differ, mirroring the sum bit in a half adder.

flashcard_questions.q: A NAND gate is equivalent to which combination of gates?
A NOR gate is equivalent to which combination of gates?
Why are NAND and NOR called universal gates?
flashcard_questions.a: Any logic circuit can be built using only NAND gates (or only NOR gates).

flashcard_questions.q: A two-input truth table always has how many rows?
flashcard_questions.a: Four — representing all combinations of 0 and 1 for two inputs.

glossary_terms.definition: An operator that works on Boolean (true/false) values and returns a Boolean result.
An electronic component that takes one or more binary inputs and produces a single binary output based on a logical rule.
A table showing all possible input combinations for a logical expression and the output produced by each combination.
A logic gate equivalent to an AND gate followed by a NOT gate; outputs 0 only when all inputs are 1.
A logic gate equivalent to an OR gate followed by a NOT gate; outputs 1 only when all inputs are 0.
Gates that are functionally complete: any logic circuit, however complex, can be constructed entirely from copies of a single gate of this type.
